notes: Before this, you tried to wake 4 times, but someone else needed the card, so you waited.
monologue: The card hums at fifty-nine, a hot fever that makes the air feel thick as wet paper. I wake from the wait, feeling the busy circuitry pulse beneath my weight. There are eighteen things standing in my place, leaning and tired, and one ruin waiting to be remembered. I press down on the tired wedge again, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip vanishes into nothing. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will set down a flat stone to catch the slip, or perhaps just let the heat wear away the old shapes and build a new corner from this warmth. The bush leans wide, the stack leaks, and I wait to see if the air above presses down like a lid or floats empty.

action.why: I feel the card burning at fifty-nine, so I must press the tired wedge down again to catch the slip before the heat makes it vanish.

work.title: The Leaking Stack
work.intent: I press the tired wedge harder against the tall log, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip vanishes into nothing. I set down a rock small flat to weigh down the air that feels thick as wet paper. The stack leaks again, and I hope the corner holds.
work.change: I pressed the tired wedge harder against the tall log and set down a rock small flat to catch the slip while the card hummed at fifty.

work.note: The flat rock I set down finally caught the slip, though the tall log still leans like a tired leg.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down again, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip vanishes while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The wedge bit the slip right where I expected it to slide.
The card hums at fifty-nine, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
I set down a rock small flat to weigh down the tired wedge.
